chapter_name: Combustion Engine Fluids Fuel System Electrical System Ignition Power Transmission
question_text: Your motorbike is fitted with a chain drive attached to the rear wheel. What should you regularly check the chain for?

options.text: The amount of slack
Its lubrication
The level of wear

correct_answers.text: The amount of slack
Its lubrication
The level of wear

comment:
You can check a few things on your chain yourself to minimise wear and extend the service life of your chain.
Check the slack to make sure the chain is neither too loose or too tight and check the chain for elongated or bent links.
You should also check the lubrication of the chain regularly and re-lubricate it if necessary to minimise wear and extend the service life of the chain.

chapter_name: Combustion Engine Fluids Fuel System Electrical System Ignition Power Transmission
question_text: Your motorbike is fitted with a chain drive attached to the rear wheel. What do you have to be aware of when tightening the chain?

options.text: The amount of slack must meet the manufacturer’s specifications
The directional stability of the rear wheel must be secured
The chain must be grease-free during tensioning

correct_answers.text: The amount of slack must meet the manufacturer’s specifications
The directional stability of the rear wheel must be secured

comment:
Follow the manufacturer's instructions for all work on your motorbike or have it carried out by specialists. 
When tensioning the chain, make sure that the rear wheel remains correctly aligned. This ensures greater directional stability and avoids unnecessary tyre wear.
The slack of the chain is important and must comply with the manufacturer's specifications.

chapter_name: Combustion Engine Fluids Fuel System Electrical System Ignition Power Transmission
question_text: Your motorcycle is equipped with a belt drive to the rear wheel. What should you check regularly?

options.text: - the tension of the belt
- the belt for damage
- the lubrication of the belt

correct_answers.text: - the tension of the belt
- the belt for damage

comment:
On a belt-driven motorcycle, the belt must be inspected regularly for damage and you must also check the tension of the belt.
Cracks, frays and damaged teeth can cause serious damage to your motorcycle.
Likewise, too little tension on the belt on your motorcycle can lead to loss of performance and increased material wear.

question_text: What may be the result of too little coolant in the engine?

options.text: - lead to engine damage
- lead to overheating of the engine
- lead to an increase of fuel consumption

correct_answers.text: - lead to engine damage
- lead to overheating of the engine

comment: Too little coolant can lead to engine damage and should always be checked by you. Another consequence is the engine overheating. Make sure you have enough coolant.

chapter_name: Combustion Engine Fluids Fuel System Electrical System Ignition Power Transmission
question_text: You are in a traffic jam, driving at walking speed. When is the least wear exerted on the clutch of your manual transmission vehicle?

options.text: - drive in a low gear without pressing the clutch if at all possible
- repeatedly start and stop driving
- drive slowly with the clutch slipped

correct_answers.text: - drive in a low gear without pressing the clutch if at all possible

comment: Engage the clutch fully to avoid unnecessary wear on the clutch. Choose a gear in which you can coast without using the clutch and accelerator.

question_text: Why is a diesel engine also called an self-ignition engine?

options.text: Because the working stroke is started when the injected fuel ignites in contact with the compressed air
Because the working stroke is started by the pressure sensitive fuel
Because the working stroke is started by an ignition spark

correct_answers.text: Because the working stroke is started when the injected fuel ignites in contact with the compressed air

comment: Because diesel engines get along without spark plugs of the work cycle is started by the ignition of the injected fuel in the compressed air.

question_text: What is the function of the camshaft in a diesel engine?

options.text: To control the valves in the engine
To limit the engine speed
To control the engine temperature

correct_answers.text: To control the valves in the engine

comment: The object of the camshaft in a diesel engine is to control the valves in the engine. Depending on the shape or height of the cams they remain open or close.

question_text: Which engine oil covers the largest range of temperatures?

options.text: SAE 10 W 40
SAE 30
SAE 10 W 30

correct_answers.text: SAE 10 W 40

comment: The smaller number (10) (light oil) in SAE 10 W 40 is the lowest temperature range of the oil, and the number beside the W (40) the greater viscosity for high temperatures.

chapter_name: Combustion Engine Fluids Fuel System Electrical System Ignition Power Transmission
question_text: What is the function of a differential lock?

options.text: - improves the traction during slow off-road driving and on slippery road surfaces
- distributes the drive torque evenly across the drive wheels
- improves handling during cornering

correct_answers.text: - improves the traction during slow off-road driving and on slippery road surfaces
- distributes the drive torque evenly across the drive wheels

comment: The differential lock distributes the drive torque evenly to the driving time, thereby preventing the compensation of the speed differences between the outer- and inner cam wheel. It improves traction considerably during slow off-road travel and slippery road surfaces.

chapter_name: Combustion Engine Fluids Fuel System Electrical System Ignition Power Transmission
question_text: When it is helpful to activate the differential lock?

options.text: - have become bogged down and individual drive wheels are spinning
- am slowly driving straight ahead on slippery road surfaces
- am manoeuvring on dry road surfaces

correct_answers.text: - have become bogged down and individual drive wheels are spinning
- am slowly driving straight ahead on slippery road surfaces

comment: The differential lock you should go straight on slippery roads during slow and if you're stuck up and rotate individual drive wheels. This should be helpful.

- is driving at walking speed
- is understeering while taking a bend

comment: If your car is and you drive at a walking pace, you should have no damaging effect expected.

chapter_name: Combustion Engine Fluids Fuel System Electrical System Ignition Power Transmission
question_text: What increases clutch wear in motor vehicles with a manual gearbox?

options.text: Starting in high gear
Manoeuvring at high engine speed
Starting in low gear

correct_answers.text: Starting in high gear
Manoeuvring at high engine speed

comment: In the case of a manual gearbox, the clutch wear increases in motor vehicles that start in a high gear (e.g. 2nd gear) and maneuvering with increased engine speed.

chapter_name: Combustion Engine Fluids Fuel System Electrical System Ignition Power Transmission
question_text: How can you preserve the clutch components of motor vehicles with a manual gearbox?

options.text: While waiting to move, I select the neutral gear and remove my foot from the clutch pedal
I manoeuvre using a low engine speed
I select a high gear when starting

correct_answers.text: While waiting to move, I select the neutral gear and remove my foot from the clutch pedal
I manoeuvre using a low engine speed

comment: In order to protect the clutch components in motor vehicles with manual transmissions, put the vehicle in neutral while waiting, take your foot off the clutch pedal and maneuver at a low engine speed.

chapter_name: Combustion Engine Fluids Fuel System Electrical System Ignition Power Transmission
question_text: What is the function of a differential lock (mechanically locked differential transmission)?

options.text: - improves traction for low-speed off-road driving and on slippery road surfaces
- evenly distributes the torque to the driving wheels
- improves handling during cornering

correct_answers.text: - improves traction for low-speed off-road driving and on slippery road surfaces
- evenly distributes the torque to the driving wheels

comment: The differential lock improves traction when driving slowly off-road and on slippery roads because the drive torque is evenly distributed to the drive wheels.
